summary: In a sparse Japanese-style dojo, Morpheus explains that the sparring program follows the same rules as the Matrix—rules like gravity—that are really computer rules which 'can be bent' and some 'can be broken,' asking 'Understand?' Neo nods. Morpheus then assumes a fighting stance and challenges him: 'Then hit me, if you can.' Neo mirrors the stance, circles cautiously, then 'he lets out a brief shriek and then unleashes a ferocious assault.' He presses a Jackie Chan-style high-speed assault of fists and feet 'from every angle,' but every single strike is deflected by effortless speed.'

what_changes.before: A trainee who has just downloaded combat skills but has not yet been told how the simulated rules actually work.
what_changes.after: Told that the program's rules are computer rules that 'can be bent' and some 'can be broken,' and that he 'must learn' this.
what_changes.evidence: What you must learn is that these

what_changes.before: Cautious and restrained, 'assumes a similar stance, cautiously circling' before committing.
what_changes.after: Commits to a full assault—'launches a furious attack'—only to have 'each and every blow... blocked by effortless speed,' revealing his attack is currently outmatched.
what_changes.evidence: he gives a short cry and launches

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus begins Neo's first sparring test inside the dojo program, explaining the bendable rules before Neo's furious attack is effortlessly blocked.

uncertain: Whether Neo ultimately lands a blow—the scene ends mid-exchange with his attacks still being blocked.
_mind_pass: ran: 1 speaker, 128w >= p75 (125w) for this work

minds.wants: To get Neo past the idea that the skills he just downloaded are the hard limit of what he can do — to make him understand, and eventually act on, the fact that the simulated rules can be bent and broken.
minds.feels: A calm, patient certainty. He has done this kind of teaching before; he is not worried about being hit because he already knows the gap between them. Under the lesson runs a quiet investment — this is the man he believes is the One, and the test is partly a genuine probe of what Neo is capable of right now.
minds.shows: Compressed instruction delivered as doctrine ('Understand?'), then an almost playful challenge ('Then hit me, if you can') and a relaxed fighting stance. He lets his effortless blocking do the talking rather than explaining further.
minds.basis: He reframes gravity as a bendable computer rule and ends the explanation with 'Understand?' — then immediately tests comprehension physically instead of lecturing. His blocking is 'effortless,' showing he is holding Neo at arm's length deliberately rather than defending for real. This follows sc-049 where Morpheus entered and said 'Show me,' establishing that he evaluates by doing.

believes_about.belief: That Neo has raw capability worth testing but has not yet grasped that the rules are bendable — that he is still fighting as if gravity and physics are real constraints.
believes_about.wrong_because: Partly true now, but Neo will internalize this far faster and more completely than Morpheus's measured pacing implies, soon bending rules in ways that outpace ordinary training.

minds.wants: To prove — to Morpheus and to himself — that the 'I know kung fu' he just declared is real, by landing a blow on the man who told him to try.
minds.feels: A rush of intoxicated confidence from the download ('I know kung fu') colliding with the first shock that confidence is not enough. The 'short cry' before he attacks is him committing, almost angrily, to prove it.
minds.shows: A nod of understanding he does not fully have, a cautious circling, then an all-out furious assault. He shows aggression and effort, not the dawning realization that effort alone is being neutralized.
minds.basis: In sc-049 he woke from the download euphoric and declared 'I know kung fu,' so he enters believing the skill is his. Here he nods at 'Understand?' before he actually does, then immediately 'launches a furious attack' — trying to win with the borrowed skill rather than with the new principle. 'Every strike is stopped with effortless speed' shows his current approach is being dismantled.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a teacher he can test himself against, and that landing a hit is a fair measure of how good he's become.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is operating on a level Neo hasn't yet been told exists; the spar isn't a fair contest and 'landing a blow' is the wrong goal until Neo learns the rules can be broken.

believes_about.belief: That possessing the downloaded techniques is the same as being able to use them effectively here.
believes_about.wrong_because: The download gave him the moves but not the understanding that the simulated physics can be bent — which is exactly why every blow is blocked.

connects_back: Neo's euphoric 'I know kung fu' in sc-049 is the confidence he is now trying to cash in during the spar.
Morpheus's 'Show me' in sc-049 establishes his pattern of testing by action, which continues as 'hit me, if you can.'
The combat-skills download (sc-048/sc-049) is what Neo is physically relying on when he launches the furious attack.
sets_up: The later dojo session (ev-014) where Morpheus brutally beats Neo to drive home that the physical disparity — and thus the rules — can be overcome only by letting go of the very limits Neo is still obeying here.
The rooftop jump training (ev-013), which applies the same 'bend the rules' principle Neo is being introduced to now.
Neo's gradual shift from relying on downloaded technique to actually bending the simulation's rules in combat.
dramatic_function: It converts the abstract promise of the combat download into a lived, physical lesson: it establishes the story's core rule — the Matrix's laws are bendable — and dramatizes the gap between having power and understanding how to wield it, so Neo's future breakthroughs feel earned rather than given.
